sdm_quotes.quote: If the NT flag is set, the IRET instruction performs a task switch (return) from a nested task (a task called with a CALL instruction, an interrupt, or an exception) back to the calling or interrupted task.
sdm_quotes.supports: NT = 1 is a task return

sdm_quotes.quote: If the return is to another privilege level, the IRET instruction also pops the stack pointer and SS from the stack, before resuming program execution.
sdm_quotes.supports: same-privilege return pops no SS:ESP

sdm_quotes.quote: IF NT = 1 THEN GOTO TASK-RETURN; (* PE = 1, VM = 0, NT = 1 *)
sdm_quotes.supports: NT is tested first, before the pops

sdm_quotes.quote: EIP := Pop(); CS := Pop(); (* 32-bit pop, high-order 16 bits discarded *) tempEFLAGS := Pop();
sdm_quotes.supports: pops: EIP, CS, EFLAGS (12 bytes)

sdm_quotes.quote: IF tempEFLAGS(VM) = 1 and CPL = 0 THEN GOTO RETURN-TO-VIRTUAL-8086-MODE; ELSE GOTO PROTECTED-MODE-RETURN;
sdm_quotes.supports: the popped VM = 1 matters only at CPL 0

sdm_quotes.quote: SWITCH-TASKS (without nesting) to TSS specified in link field of current TSS;
sdm_quotes.supports: the task return switches to the TSS named by the link field

sdm_quotes.quote: IF CS(RPL) > CPL THEN GOTO RETURN-TO-OUTER-PRIVILEGE-LEVEL; ELSE GOTO RETURN-TO-SAME-PRIVILEGE-LEVEL; FI;
sdm_quotes.supports: RPL = CPL = 3 is the same-privilege return

sdm_quotes.quote: IF EIP is not within CS limit THEN #GP(0); FI;
sdm_quotes.supports: EIP beyond the CS limit (4 GB for the derived code descriptors)

sdm_quotes.quote: EFLAGS (CF, PF, AF, ZF, SF, TF, DF, OF, NT) := tempEFLAGS;
sdm_quotes.supports: loaded flags

sdm_quotes.quote: IF OperandSize = 32 or OperandSize = 64 THEN EFLAGS(RF, AC, ID) := tempEFLAGS; FI;
sdm_quotes.supports: RF, AC, ID are loaded for a 32-bit operand

sdm_quotes.quote: IF CPL ≤ IOPL THEN EFLAGS(IF) := tempEFLAGS; FI;
sdm_quotes.supports: IF only if CPL <= IOPL

sdm_quotes.quote: IF CPL = 0 THEN EFLAGS(IOPL) := tempEFLAGS;
sdm_quotes.supports: IOPL only at CPL 0

sdm_quotes.quote: IF OperandSize = 32 or OperandSize = 64 THEN EFLAGS(VIF, VIP) := tempEFLAGS; FI; FI;
sdm_quotes.supports: VIF, VIP only at CPL 0

sdm_quotes.quote: #GP(0) If the return code or stack segment selector is NULL.
sdm_quotes.supports: null CS: #GP(0)

sdm_quotes.quote: #GP(selector) If a segment selector index is outside its descriptor table limits.
sdm_quotes.supports: TI = 1 (null LDTR) or beyond the GDT limit: #GP(selector)

sdm_quotes.quote: If the return code segment selector RPL is less than the CPL.
sdm_quotes.supports: RPL < CPL: #GP(selector)

sdm_quotes.quote: If the DPL of a conforming-code segment is greater than the return code segment selector RPL.
sdm_quotes.supports: conforming with DPL > RPL: #GP(selector)

sdm_quotes.quote: If the DPL for a nonconforming-code segment is not equal to the RPL of the code segment selector.
sdm_quotes.supports: non-conforming with DPL != RPL: #GP(selector)

sdm_quotes.quote: If the segment descriptor for a code segment does not indicate it is a code segment.
sdm_quotes.supports: not a code segment: #GP(selector)

sdm_quotes.quote: #NP (selector) If the return code segment is not present.
sdm_quotes.supports: not present: #NP(selector)

sdm_quotes.quote: If the segment selector for a TSS has its local/global bit set for local.
sdm_quotes.supports: a task-return link selector with TI = 1: #GP(selector)

sdm_quotes.quote: If a TSS segment descriptor specifies that the TSS is not busy.
sdm_quotes.supports: a TSS descriptor that is not busy (the available double-fault and NMI TSS): #GP(selector)

sdm_quotes.quote: Checks that the new task is available (call, jump, exception, or interrupt) or busy (IRET return).
sdm_quotes.supports: an IRET return needs a busy TSS

sdm_quotes.quote: If software uses an IRET instruction to suspend the new task, the processor checks for EFLAGS.NT = 1; it then uses the value in the previous task link field to return to the previous task.
sdm_quotes.supports: the link field is the return target

sdm_quotes.quote: When a CALL instruction, an interrupt, or an exception causes a task switch: the processor copies the segment selector for the current TSS to the previous task link field of the TSS for the new task; it then sets EFLAGS.NT = 1.
sdm_quotes.supports: the only hardware store of the link field (backlink)

sdm_quotes.quote: To keep such spurious task switches from succeeding, the operating system should initialize the previous task link field in every TSS that it creates to 0.
sdm_quotes.supports: the OS convention for the link field

sdm_quotes.quote: If a POPF/POPFD instruction is executed with ... privilege, an exception does not occur but privileged bits do not change.
sdm_quotes.supports: POPFD at CPL 3: the privileged bits (IF, IOPL) stay; NT is not one of them

sdm_quotes.quote: 32, 64 1-3 <CPL S N N S N 0 S N S S N S S S S S S
sdm_quotes.supports: Table 1-12: protected mode, 32-bit operand, CPL 1-3 with IOPL < CPL: NT (7th flag column) is S (modified)

sdm_quotes.quote: Bits 1, 3, 5, 15, and 22 through 31 of this register are reserved.
sdm_quotes.supports: bit 1 is reserved; IRET loads only the flags it names

ds.source: Intel SDM Vol 3A 3.4.2 and Vol 2B MOV Sreg protected-mode: DS/ES/FS/GS load a data segment or a readable code segment whose DPL >= max(CPL, RPL) (a conforming code segment: no DPL test); GDT[0x18] is the ring-3 code segment (type 0xA: execute/read, non-conforming, DPL 3, present, base 0, limit 4 GB), 0x20 the ring-3 data segment, 0x38 the TEB segment, 0x40 a DPL 3 read/write data segment (rows gdt.descriptors); every RPL 0-3 passes the DPL 3 test; the null selectors 0-3 load (the register becomes null, SDM Vol 3A 3.4.2)

gp_selector_descriptors.source: Intel SDM Vol 3A 3.4.2 and Vol 2B MOV Sreg protected-mode: a code segment of DPL < max(CPL, RPL) that is not conforming (DS/ES/FS/GS) or a system descriptor is #GP(selector); GDT descriptors derived in rows gdt.descriptors and gdt_writes

rule.ldt_descriptor_0x48: GDT[0x48] is written only by a process switch to a process that has an LDT (KiLoadLdtr / KiSwapProcess, row ldt): then it is a system descriptor (type 2), #GP(selector); otherwise it is zero (#NP is not modelled): in both cases the load faults

null_ss.source: Intel SDM Vol 3A 3.4.2 and Vol 2B MOV Sreg protected-mode: loading the null selector into SS is #GP(0)

ss_rpl_ne_cpl_or_dpl.source: Intel SDM Vol 3A 3.4.2 and Vol 2B MOV Sreg protected-mode: SS needs RPL = CPL and DPL = CPL; a selector of any other RPL, a data segment of another DPL, or a segment that is not writable data (code, system) is #GP(selector)

ti1.selectors: every selector value with bit 2 (TI) set
ti1.source: Intel SDM Vol 3A 3.4.2 and Vol 2B MOV Sreg protected-mode: a selector in the LDT is checked against the LDT limit; the LDTR is null (row ldt.rule and sldt: a new process has the null LDTR, so every TI=1 selector indexes an empty table), so the limit is exceeded: #GP(selector)

undecided_descriptors.why: inside the GDT limit but not built by winload nor written by a decoded kernel path; the content is not derived, so the fault kind (#GP or #NP) and a possible load are not decided. No consumer treats them as loadable

ss.source: Intel SDM Vol 3A 3.4.2 and Vol 2B MOV Sreg protected-mode: SS needs RPL = CPL = 3 and a writable data segment of DPL 3 (GDT 0x20, 0x38, 0x40, rows gdt.descriptors); the null selector is #GP(0); a code segment (0x18) is #GP(selector)

undecided.why: every selector value the record can decide is decided by the rows above; the ones whose GDT descriptor is not derived are in `undecided_descriptors` (none of them is loadable here: the consumers fault on them)

null_seg_access.faults: an instruction with a memory operand whose segment register (default or by prefix) holds the null selector; lea, and a prefixed instruction without a memory operand, do not fault

base.why: SGDT at CPL 3 stores the GDTR base of the processor the thread runs on. That address is not a function of fixed inputs: the BSP's GDT is the page winload's boot-library page allocator returns (BlMmAllocatePages with no requested address, searching the boot memory descriptor lists), and every application processor's GDT is the block MmAllocateIndependentPages returns (system PTE reservation) plus a constant. Both depend on the machine's memory map and on allocations made before the thread runs. No base is given
